A1.justification: Both complete, readable 20-page PDFs describe the same REFDIV study, with matching authors, main sections and Appendices A–J. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original REFDIV experiments on AdvBench, including attack success rates, transferability, defense evaluations and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main comparisons in Table 1 and additional experiments and analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: REFDIV's genetic algorithm, reference-guided entropy objective, dynamic weighting and inference procedure remain unchanged in Section 3, Algorithm 1 and Appendix E.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same AdvBench coverage, cross-TTS and closed-source transfer scenarios, and defense evaluations. No dataset, task or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains GCG, AutoDAN and AutoDAN-Turbo. Comparator membership in the corresponding appendix experiments, including AutoDAN comparisons, is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation settings are unchanged: AdvBench's 520 queries, ASR evaluation, Best-of-N with N = 2, 8 and 16, MCTS budgets, and decoding and optimization settings.

E4.justification: Candidate-count and reward-model analyses, transferability case studies, perplexity filtering, MCTS and weighting-schedule sensitivity, and entropy–ASR analyses are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Statistical and uncertainty reporting remains unchanged, including the plotted bands and Appendix H correlation analysis. No repeated-run or seed disclosure, confidence interval or significance test is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical and qualitative results in Tables 1–10 and Figures 2–14 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains REFDIV's Llama3.1-8B ASR of 0.465 for Best-of-N and 0.967 for MCTS.

T1.justification: The LLM, TTS and ASR definitions, entropy-based fitness equation, and appendix weighting-schedule formulas are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about diversity suppression, TTS safety failures, REFDIV's transferability and the limited effectiveness of evaluated defenses.

C2.justification: The explanations of REFDIV's mechanism, transferability differences, entropy–safety relationship and mitigation limitations remain unchanged. No substantive qualification or applicability boundary is introduced.

D1.justification: Appendix J in v3 adds a pointer to the SKNahin/RefDiv repository for additional details and code, absent from v2. Existing implementation details and hyperparameters are unchanged; repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations and the reference list retain the same works and research positioning. The updated publication notice does not alter the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 replaces the preprint notice with an ICML 2026 proceedings and copyright notice and adds the repository sentence in Appendix J. The scientific narrative and section hierarchy remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The Introduction moves from below the abstract to the right column on page 1, with associated spacing and column/page reflow. Figures and tables retain their designs and contents.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer in Appendix J modestly improves reproducibility guidance by identifying where readers can seek code and additional details. Scientific evidence and claims remain unchanged. This benefit concerns access information; the PDFs do not verify the repository's contents or functionality.
